text:
I'm going to post a short team message with the lessons from this game. The main one is that I discarded eleven cards, far too many, and that habit of discarding to regain a clue cost us important cards. Several early discards of cards I hadn't identified turned out to be needed, so I should only discard cards known to be dead or proven unnecessary, and use clues more actively to pin down which ranks are playable.

I'm going to check whether the next step is to post one message, since only A02 writes the brain and I can offer suggestions.

args.text: A03 retro, game 1 (22/35). What worked: rank signals on a tower's next rank ("2", "3", "1") made the holder play at once; slot-by-slot deduction from the unseen-card list was exact late. What cost us: 11 discards. Most were blind drops to refill signals (Violet 2, Rose 7, Moss 5, Violet 5, Cobalt 4) and several were cards we later needed. Proposal: discard only when a card is provably dead or when 0 signals are left and nobody can use a signal; never discard an unknown card to "get a signal" unless the pile is nearly empty. Also: a teammate who sees a playable card in your hand should signal at once, and we should spend signals early on next-rank ranks rather than sit on them.
